name: 0xword
description: Guess 8 hex digits that make a real 4-letter word, then decode it. In your side bar while your agent works.

enumDescriptions: Show nothing when your agent starts working. Your agent hooks can stay set up.
Show the notices switched on below while your agent works, and remove them when it finishes.

Agent-driven: when your agent's hooks report that it has started working, 0xWORD waits Delay Seconds, then opens its panel and starts a new round if none is in progress. A round in progress is kept as it is. If your agent finishes first, nothing opens. Shows none of the notices.
0xword.autoStart.mode.markdownDescription: What 0xWORD does when your agent starts working. Notices are `off` by default, so nothing shows. Choose `notify` to turn them on, or `open` to open the panel once your agent has worked for a while. `open` is agent-driven: when your agent's hooks report it has started, 0xWORD waits `delaySeconds`, then opens the panel and starts a new round if none is in progress. A round in progress is kept as it is.

0xword.autoStart.delaySeconds.markdownDescription: Only in `open` mode: how many seconds your agent works before the 0xWORD panel opens, so quick prompts never interrupt you. `0` opens it at once. Up to 3600 (an hour); any other value uses 20.

0xword.notify.badge.markdownDescription: In `notify` mode, show a badge on the 0xWORD icon in the activity bar while your agent works. It shows once you've opened the 0xWORD panel since VS Code started.

0xword.notify.statusBar.markdownDescription: In `notify` mode, show `0x Round ready` in the status bar while your agent works. Click it to open the panel.

0xword.notify.popup.markdownDescription: In `notify` mode, show a notification with **Play** and **Not now** when your agent starts working. It's a normal VS Code notification, so it doesn't take keyboard focus.
